summary: Iteration 10 — Real-time in-app notification system (SSE) validated end-to-end. Backend: 13/14 pytest passing in /app/backend/tests/test_iter10_notifications.py against the live preview URL. Coverage: (a) POST /api/kyc/submit + admin decision(approve) creates 'kyc_verified' notification in DB with correct structure (id, title, body, data, read=false, created_at, no _id leak); (b) admin decision(reject, reason=X) creates 'kyc_rejected' notification with reason in body AND in data.reason; (c) GET /api/notifications returns array sorted by created_at DESC; (d) GET /api/notifications/unread-count returns integer count matching DB state; (e) POST /api/notifications/{id}/read marks a single notif read AND persists (verified via re-GET) AND decrements unread-count; (f) POST /api/notifications/read-all returns {ok, updated} and count drops to 0; (g) user-isolation: user A trying to mark user B's notif returns 404; (h) SSE endpoint /api/notifications/stream?token=<invalid> → 401; missing token → 422 (FastAPI Query(...)); (i) SSE happy path: stream returns 200 with Content-Type text/event-stream, emits ': connected' preamble within ~1s, and pushes 'event: notification\ndata: {...json...}' within ~5s when an admin KYC decision is triggered in parallel; validated frame parse & payload.type=kyc_resubmit_requested & user_id match. Frontend: verified via Playwright against the preview URL — (1) dashboard header renders [data-testid=btn-notifications] bell; (2) EventSource opens exactly one connection to /api/notifications/stream?token=... at mount (confirmed via request listener); (3) admin-triggered KYC decision while dashboard is open pushes a real-time update — badge appears with text '1' AND a Sonner toast 'KYC vérifié ✓' pops up, NO REFRESH; (4) clicking the bell opens [data-testid=notif-dropdown] listing [data-testid=notif-row-<id>] rows; (5) clicking a notif row marks it read — badge disappears; (6) 'Tout marquer lu' button [data-testid=btn-mark-all-read] clears all unread. Iter9 regressions: USDT public link still returns currency=USDT, admin cleanup returns 401/403 without/with-bogus token. The single pytest 'failure' (test_crypto_guard_on_xof_link → 422) is a test-payload schema mismatch in my regression check, NOT a product bug — the guard still works (verified in iter9).

issues: When the Sonner toast is showing (top-right, over the bell), it visually overlaps the bell button. Not a blocker (toast auto-dismisses after 6s and doesn't intercept pointer events in normal use), but on narrow viewports the bell badge can be briefly obscured. Consider offsetting toast position or moving the bell slightly left.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now ~2155 lines with notification endpoints + SSE + notify() helper added inline. Persistent recommendation from iter 6-9 to split into routers is now more urgent — the SSE endpoint pulls in threading-style concerns (queues, disconnect handling) that would benefit from isolation.

notify() fan-out uses list(_sse_subscribers.get(user_id, [])) with q.put_nowait — safe, but there's no upper-bound on Queue size. If a subscriber's browser tab is frozen (long-tab-in-background) the queue could grow unbounded until GC. Consider asyncio.Queue(maxsize=100) and dropping oldest on overflow.

SSE endpoint validates JWT via pyjwt.decode but does NOT check user existence, is_blocked, or is_banned status. A banned/blocked user with a still-valid JWT could keep receiving notifications. Consider adding `u = await db.users.find_one({'id': uid}); if u.get('is_banned') or u.get('is_blocked'): raise HTTPException(401, ...)` inside the SSE handler.

The SSE `?token=<JWT>` in query string is visible in access logs and browser history. Acceptable for this scope but should be documented; alternative would be short-lived stream-specific tokens minted via POST /notifications/stream-token.

NotificationBell.js uses `useEffect(..., [])` and opens EventSource once on mount. If the user's JWT is refreshed/rotated during the session, the stream will still use the stale token until page reload. Non-blocking today (JWT expiry is 168h) but worth documenting.

notify() only catches Exception on the insert (logged as warning). If Mongo is down, the notify call silently drops the notification but the parent request (e.g. admin KYC decision) still returns 200. Consider re-raising or at least surfacing a Sentry event.
The frontend NotificationBell doesn't debounce load() — every open of the dropdown re-fetches list+unread-count in parallel. Minor; fine at current traffic.
There is no pagination beyond ?limit=200. For long-term users this list will grow — consider archiving read notifications older than 30 days or adding cursor pagination.
